title: Smooth affine concentrators of smooth invariant closed subschemes
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $X$ be an affine finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] smooth over $k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], with an action of $\mathbf G_{m,k}$ [def-sc-gm-ga]. An action is a morphism $\mu:\mathbf G_m\times_k X\to X$ satisfying the unit and associativity identities. Let $Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a smooth closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion], invariant under this action. For a commutative $k$-algebra $R$ and $x\in X(R)$, say that $\lim_{t\to0}t\cdot x$ exists if the orbit map $\mathbf G_{m,R}\to X_R$ extends to $\mathbf A^1_R\to X_R$, and define the limit to be its value at zero. The functor
$$R\longmapsto\{x\in X(R):\lim_{t\to0}t\cdot x\text{ exists and lies in }Z(R)\}$$
is represented by a smooth closed subscheme $X(Z)\hookrightarrow X$ of finite type over $k$. The extension is unique, and evaluation at zero defines a morphism $X(Z)\to Z$. These assertions hold for all commutative test algebras, including nonreduced ones.

source.place: Definition 13.21, Proposition 13.23 and Proposition 13.24, printed pp.261--262; smoothness follows from Proposition 13.22, proved by graded local algebra in Lemmas 13.25--13.27, pp.262--263.

proof.text: Write $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak a)$. The action gives a coaction $c:A\to A[t,t^{-1}]$. For $f\in A$, write $c(f)=\sum_n f_n t^n$. Coassociativity, by comparison of the coefficients of $s^it^j$, gives $c(f_n)=f_nt^n$; the counit gives $f=\sum_n f_n$. Uniqueness of Laurent coefficients makes this a direct sum $A=\bigoplus_n A_n$, and multiplicativity gives $A_iA_j\subseteq A_{i+j}$. Invariance of $Z$ means $c(\mathfrak a)\subseteq\mathfrak a[t,t^{-1}]$, so every homogeneous component of an element of $\mathfrak a$ belongs to $\mathfrak a$. Put $\mathfrak b=(\mathfrak a\cap A_0,\bigcup_{n<0}A_n)$ and $B=A/\mathfrak b$. The quotient $B$ is nonnegatively graded. Its spectrum $Y$ is a closed subscheme of $X$ of finite type: any finite set of $k$-algebra generators of $A$ maps to generators of $B$.

source.place: Definition 13.21 and the preceding coaction/gradation discussion, printed pp.260--261; coefficient calculation written out

proof.text: For every commutative $k$-algebra $R$, a point $x:A\to R$ has orbit homomorphism $f\mapsto\sum_n x(f_n)t^n$. The inclusion $R[t]\hookrightarrow R[t,t^{-1}]$ is injective, even when $R$ has nilpotents, because Laurent monomials are an $R$-basis. This homomorphism lands in $R[t]$ exactly when $x(A_n)=0$ for all $n<0$. Then its evaluation at zero is $f\mapsto x(f_0)$ and factors through $A/\mathfrak a$ exactly when $x(\mathfrak a\cap A_0)=0$, since $\mathfrak a$ is homogeneous. These two conditions are precisely $x(\mathfrak b)=0$. The extension is unique by injectivity. Thus $Y$ represents the required functor on all test algebras. The map $A\to B$, $f\mapsto\overline{f_0}$, is multiplicative: in the degree-zero part of a product every term of nonzero paired degrees has a negative-degree factor killed in $B$. It kills $\mathfrak a$ and therefore gives a morphism $\pi:Y\to Z$, functorially the limit.

source.place: Proposition 13.24 and equation (85), printed pp.260--262; polynomial coefficient proof over arbitrary R

proof.text: The equations commute with every field extension $K/k$. Indeed tensoring the direct sums gives the same degree components, and the ideal generated by $\mathfrak a_0$ and the negative components becomes its extended ideal. Hence $Y_K=\operatorname{Spec}(K\otimes_kB)$ is the same construction for $(X_K,Z_K)$. Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-large-algclosed-jacobson] to $Y$: choose an algebraically closed extension $K/k$ such that every closed subset of $Y_K$ has a dense set of closed points and every closed point has residue field $K$. By [lem-pc-proper-base-change], $X_K$ and $Z_K$ are smooth. Their local rings are regular by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular]. Work over $K$ in the next three steps, using $A,\mathfrak a,\mathfrak b,B$ for the base-changed coordinate rings and ideals.

source.place: Proposition 13.23, printed p.261, reduction to an algebraically closed field

proof.text: Let $y$ be a closed point of $Y$ and set $z=\pi(y)\in Z(K)$. The degree-zero evaluation defining $z$ kills every nonzero degree in $A$, so $z$ is fixed, also as a point of $Y$. Let $\mathfrak p_z=\ker(A\to K)$ and $\mathfrak p_0=\mathfrak p_z\cap A_0$. Put $S=A_0\setminus\mathfrak p_0$ and $D=S^{-1}A$, graded using degree-zero denominators. Now $D_0=(A_0)_{\mathfrak p_0}$ is local and $\mathfrak m=S^{-1}\mathfrak p_z=\mathfrak p_0D_0\oplus\bigoplus_{n\ne0}D_n$ is a maximal ideal with residue $K$. This equality follows by evaluating at $z$ degree by degree. The ring $A$ is Noetherian by [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components]; $D$ is Noetherian since any ideal of $D$ is generated by images of generators of its contracted ideal in $A$. The ideal $\mathfrak aD$ is homogeneous and contained in $\mathfrak m$. Its degree-zero component is $S^{-1}\mathfrak a_0$; the ideal generated by it and the negative components of $D$ is $\mathfrak bD$. Finally $D_{\mathfrak m}=A_{\mathfrak p_z}$ and $(D/\mathfrak aD)_{\mathfrak m/\mathfrak aD}=(A/\mathfrak a)_{\mathfrak p_z/\mathfrak a}$, by inverting the same elements in two stages. Both are regular by step 3. Apply [lem-sfb-graded-local-attraction-regularity]: its conclusion is exactly regularity of $B_{\mathfrak p_z/\mathfrak b}$, the local ring of $Y$ at $z$.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 13.22 after Lemma 13.27, printed p.263; the degree-zero localization and its hypotheses made explicit

proof.text: Because $z$ is a $K$-rational closed point and $K$ is algebraically closed, [lem-weil-pbc-regular-closed-point-smooth-source] gives smoothness of $B/K$ at $z$. With [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] this gives an open neighbourhood $U$ of $z$ in $Y$ smooth over $K$. The extended orbit of $y$ is $\alpha:\mathbf A^1_K\to Y$: its polynomial coefficients annihilate the homogeneous ideal $\mathfrak b$, so it really lands in $Y$, and $\alpha(0)=z$. The open set $\alpha^{-1}(U)$ contains zero, hence contains $D(h)$ for a polynomial $h$ with $h(0)\ne0$. Since $K$ is infinite, there is $c\in K^\times$ with $h(c)\ne0$. Thus $c\cdot y\in U$. Multiplication by $c$ is an automorphism of $Y$ with inverse multiplication by $c^{-1}$ (the ideal $\mathfrak b$ is homogeneous). Transporting this smooth open neighbourhood by that inverse shows $Y$ is smooth at $y$.

source.place: Proposition 13.22, printed pp.261--263; explicit passage from the regular limit point to its orbit

proof.text: Let $V$ be the union of all smooth open neighbourhoods of points of $Y$. Every closed point lies in $V$ by steps 4--5. If the closed complement $Y\setminus V$ were nonempty, the density clause of [lem-sfb-scheme-large-algclosed-jacobson] would give a closed point in it, a contradiction. Thus these smooth opens cover $Y$. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-local-on-source], $Y_K$ is smooth over $K$, including when $Y_K$ is empty.

source.place: Proposition 13.23, printed p.261; closed-point argument and source-local smoothness

proof.text: Return to $k$. The finite-type algebra $B$ is finitely presented over the field $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation], so $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally finitely presented. The field-extension map $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is flat and surjective by [lem-pc-field-extension-flat] and [lem-pc-field-extension-surjective]. Its base change $Y_K\to Y$ is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. For each $v\in Y$, choose $v_K$ above it. Step 6 and [lem-sfb-scheme-lfp-smooth-flat-base-change] imply smoothness at $v$. These smooth open neighbourhoods cover $Y$, so [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-local-on-source] gives smoothness over $k$. Combined with steps 1--2 this proves all assertions, with no reducedness restriction on the test algebra.

source.place: Proposition 13.23, printed p.261; explicit flat descent of pointwise smoothness

The item statement is unchanged (identical to clones/live, where the item is still unsplit with no proof). Milne's grading convention f(tx)=Σf_n(x)t^n matches the delivery's coaction. Steps 1-2 are correct elementary work: Laurent-coefficient uniqueness over any R, including nilpotents and R=0, and f↦f̄_0 is multiplicative modulo b. Step 3: the Jacobson node gives clauses (i) and (ii), proper-base-change clause (2) and smooth-over-field-regular give regularity. Step 4: z is fixed, p_z=p_0⊕⊕_{n≠0}A_n, the localization at A_0∖p_0 makes m an ideal, and a⊆p_z, so the new lemma applies with exactly its hypotheses. Step 5 writes out the orbit propagation: h(0)≠0, an infinite field gives c, and scaling by c is a K-automorphism of Y. Steps 6-7: closed-point density, then descent via lfp + flat + surjective with the pointwise criterion. The new node is Milne 13.27 (Hesselink 5.6) as statement only. Its explicit ideal hypothesis on m is needed: K[u,v] with weights ±1 and A_0 localized at (uv−1) has A_0 local but m not proper. I tested it on a=0 with weights ±1 and on trivial gradings. It is true, not a clause of the item, and not a duplicate of positive-graded-regular-polynomial, regular-quotient-parameter-approximation or torus-fixed-scheme-smooth. No SGA. Batch 5: the cited lfp-smooth-flat-base-change reaches lem-trf-smooth-at-point-fibre-criterion, which is the generic flat-fibre smoothness criterion and no part of the trace-formula or Poincaré-duality proofs; torus-fixed-scheme-smooth already cites it. Accepted. The generic AG tool_uses are accepted.
